nodes.text: Let $R(k)$ be the Ramsey number for $K_k$, the minimal $n$ such that every $2$-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$. Give a constructive proof that $R(k)>C^k$ for some constant $C>1$.

#78 : [Er69b] [Er71] [Er88] [Er93,p.337] [Er95] [Er97c] [Va99,3.49] graph theory | ramsey theory Erdős gave a simple probabilistic proof that $R(k) \gg k2^{k/2}$. Equivalently, this question asks for an explicit construction of a graph on $n$ vertices which does not contain any clique or independent set of size $\geq c\log n$ for some constant $c>0$. In [Er69b] Erdős asks for even a construction whose largest clique or independent set has size $o(n^{1/2})$, which is now known. Cohen [Co15] (see the introduction for further history) constructed a graph on $n$ vertices which does not contain any clique or independent set of size\[\geq 2^{(\log\log n)^{C}}\]for some constant $C>0$. Li [Li23b] has recently improved this to\[\geq (\log n)^{C}\]for some constant $C>0$. This problem is #4 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
